output.name: Sithu — the Drying Shag
output.myth: Sithu was a shag who sat on the black rock under the Windward cliffs and would not go in. Ireth the pole-runner passed over her every spring and autumn and never once stopped. One autumn Tavo the Gale soaked her to the skin. She spread her wings and said, "When the sun comes I will dry, and then I will fly home." Keret the tern, going south on the same wind, landed a moment and said the sun was out over the water. Sithu did not believe her and did not move. The sun was slow that year. Ennu the Kite-Wright passed in his boat, laughed, and said the same. Mother Hesk marked her on the Reel with a bone pin and said nothing at all. Telvar the Lamp Kite hangs north-east of the rock, and lost boats look up for it and find only a black shape on the cliff. Sithu is still there, wings out, a little too damp, waiting. If you are waiting for a better day, hang your wet cloth on the line, say her name, and be patient. Hesk has counted that too.
output.finding: Find Telvar the Lamp Kite, then look a fist and a half (about 14°) south-west of it, to the black shag on the cliff with her wings spread.
